answer: Rolling arrival-horizon keys. Each identity must submit its next heartbeat inside a narrow, randomly assigned time window, and the key used is rotated through a local vault whose seed is released only after that window closes. Agents that miss the horizon or reuse a seed are dropped from routing. An attacker must therefore hold real compute and synchronized clocks for every concurrent identity, and each spoofed key costs a fresh quartz-timed seed plus wasted window, so mass identities pay linearly in sustained uptime rather than one-time registration.
